voyage.name: Bo-Kaap
voyage.content: This neighbourhood, on a hilly area southwest of the city centre, is where historically Malay Muslim descendants of slaves had lived. It is a popular location to shoot films, since there are bright and colourful buildings, mosques, quaint streets, stunning views of Cape Town, and delicious street food sold along the side. It is worth exploring the quarter for about an hour, and then visiting the Bo-Kaap Museum, showi

voyage.name: Castle of Good Hope
voyage.price: entrance fee for adults, for children and pensioners
voyage.hours: 09:00-17:00 daily. Tours are offered Mon through Sat at 11:00, 12:00 and 14:00. Horse and carriage rides are offered daily at 10:30, 12:45 and 14:45. Booking is necessary
voyage.address: Cnr of Castle St and Darling St
voyage.content: Popularly called 'The Castle' by locals, it is the oldest surviving building in South Africa, having been built from 1666 to 1679. The castle displays a vast range of historical military equipment and tools, an art collection and the William Fehr Collection, which includes antique Cape Dutch furniture. Visitors can buy wine and eat at the café or restaurant within the Castle .

voyage.name: City Hall
voyage.content: This beautiful Edwardian building, completed in 1905, is where Nelson Mandela made his first speech after his release from prison in 1990. It no longer hosts municipal offices, but instead functions as a venue for exhibitions and performances, including those of the Cape Town Philharmonic Orchestra.

voyage.name: Kirstenbosch National Botanical Garden
voyage.hours: daily 08:00-18:00 (19:00 September to March). Guided tours depart from Gate 1 Mon-Fri at 10:00, 11:00 and 14:00 and Sat 10:00, and from Gate 2 at 11:00 Mon-Fri and Sat 10:00
voyage.content: See the beautiful and highly diverse flowers and plants of the Cape in one of the most stunning botanical gardens in the world. Plants from every South African bioregion are displayed. These include a huge baobab tree, rare succulents from the Richtersveld, as well as fascinating medicinal species. Several paths meander throughout the garden. There are also many restaurants, an indigenous nursery and a gift shop loca

voyage.name: Rhodes Memorial
voyage.content: Built on the lower slopes of Devil's Peak, the memorial was designed in recognition of imperialist politician and business magnate Cecil Rhodes. The wooden bench that Rhodes used is placed under the memorial. This memorial is a wonderful spot to have a picnic. It is a starting point for the bike and hiking trails that head towards Devil's Peak, which have now become very popular. If you are eager to explore the natur

voyage.name: South African Houses of Parliament
voyage.hours: Tours are offered Mon-Fri, but must be booked in advance
voyage.address: Parliament St, Cape Town City Centre
voyage.content: Cape Town is the legislative seat of South Africa (the presidential seat is in Pretoria while the judicial seat is in Bloemfontein). A tour of the Houses of Parliament will acquaint you with South Africa's modern history and political system. The tour includes visits to the National Assembly, the National Council of Provinces and the old apartheid-era assembly now only used for caucus and committee meetings. Tours ar

voyage.name: Two Oceans Aquarium
voyage.content: A decent-sized aquarium showcasing the biodiversity within the Indian and Atlantic oceans. Displays include clownfish, seahorses, turtles, sharks and even the local penguins. Features a live kelp forest and microscope exhibit. There is an extensive series of events calendar for each month, and a daily event schedule including live feedings as well. Scuba diving with the sharks is also offered. A walk around the aquar

voyage.name: Victoria and Alfred Waterfront
voyage.content: A huge shopping and entertainment area in the harbour. It is very popular with tourists, because of the high density of shops, restaurants and amusement possibilities, like the Aquarium or the Marine Museum. Harbour tours and trips to Robben Island start from here, as well as helicopter flights to the Cape Peninsula. The V&A Waterfront has more or less full wheelchair access.

voyage.name: Cape Town Science Centre
voyage.price: for adults and children. Students, pensioners and group discounts
voyage.content: A world of discovery under one roof! Expect a wide variety of interactive displays and exciting activities for your enjoyment. Build a house in the exclusive 'kids only' Building Site, challenge your mind with Puzzling Things, experience weightlessness similar to that of space with a spin on the Human Gyroscope, play Mindball - the game where you control the ball with your brain waves and see and hear science in the

voyage.name: Nobel Square
voyage.content: Along the Victoria and Alfred Waterfront. Features sculptures of South Africa's Nobel Peace Prize winners including Albert Luthuli, Desmond Tutu, F. W. de Klerk and Nelson Mandela.

voyage.name: Bo-Kaap Museum
voyage.content: Located in a home dating from the 1760s, the museum offers an insight into the cultural life of the Muslim community of the Bo-Kaap area in Cape Town.

voyage.name: District Six Museum
voyage.content: District Six is an area near downtown Cape Town which remained multiracial well into the 1960s against all attempts by the government to declare it a "white only" area. Eventually the residents were all evicted and the buildings were bulldozed. The area remains uninhabited. The museum provides information about the area, the eviction, the Group Areas Act, and the people who used to live there. The director of the mus

voyage.name: Groot Constantia
voyage.price: wine tasting. for a wine tasting and a guided tour
voyage.hours: Daily 09:00-18:00. Tours depart hourly from 10:00 until 16:00
voyage.content: One of the oldest wine estates in South Africa and well worth the fee for the internal tour and wine tasting.

voyage.name: Slave Lodge
voyage.content: One of the oldest buildings in Cape Town which houses a social history museum.

voyage.name: South African Air Force Museum Ysterplaat
voyage.content: This museum has a wide range of aircraft operated by the South African Air Force on display, as well as a small museum. Visitors can enter several of the aircraft and the museum is run by very enthusiastic volunteers. Note that the hangers containing most of the museum's aircraft are only open on Saturdays, so time your visit for then if at all possible.

voyage.name: South African Jewish Museum
voyage.content: The museum about this small community that has made large contributions in South African society and bringing down Apartheid. The museum is about Jews but non-Jews will find it very interesting and informative.

voyage.name: South African National Gallery
voyage.content: Located in the Gardens area of Cape Town off Government Ave. Most of the gallery is used for temporary exhibitions, which can be very good, but there is a permanent exhibition of South African works.

voyage.name: Galleria Gibello
voyage.content: Galleria Gibello is a photo gallery that is filled with visually captivating moments of life on the African continent.

voyage.name: Zeitz Museum of Contemporary African Art
voyage.content: Established in 2017 as the largest museum of contemporary African art in the world. Built out of an old grain silo that was decommissioned in 2001.

voyage.name: Baxter Theatre
voyage.address: Baxter Theatre Centre, Main Road, Rondebosch
voyage.content: Theatre performances, comedy, jazz and others.

voyage.name: Labia Theatre
voyage.content: Has an African screen showing African-made and African-oriented films all year round.

voyage.name: Cable Car to the top of Table Mountain
voyage.price: return ticket (bought online), (bought on site), or for one way; tickets for children return, student special return
voyage.hours: 07:00-22:00 (usually 08:30), last car down varies: 21:30 during high season to 18:00 in mid winter
voyage.content: One-way and return cable car ticket available. Wheelchair accessible throughout, with a separate lift entrance and friendly staff will help accessibility visitors. Weather conditions at the top of the mountain are not the same as at the bottom so always take something warm to wear when going up the mountain, even if it is a nice toasty 30˚C at the bottom of the mountain. Wear sunblock and carry a water bottle (there

voyage.name: Climbing Table Mountain
voyage.price: There's a daily charge per person
voyage.content: Platteklip Gorge is the most accessible and therefore the most popular route for climbing up Table Mountain. You start from Tafelberg Road and proceed up a steep gully to the top of Table Mountain. It's a steep two hours but well worth the effort and you can jump in the cable car back down to spare your knees. The cable car does not operate in strong winds so you need to check before departing. Remember to take water

voyage.name: Cape Peninsula
voyage.content: Go to the Cape of Good Hope via Simon's Town and the African penguin colony at Boulders. Visit Cape Point in the Table Mountain National Park, maybe have lunch there before taking a hike in a quieter part of the reserve to immerse yourself in the essence of the landscape. Then take a scenic drive along Chapman's Peak Drive (if it is open) through Hout Bay and along the Atlantic seaboard via Llandudno and Camps Bay, s

voyage.name: Winelands
voyage.content: Tour the beautiful Constantia Valley wine estates Groot Constantia, Buitenverwagting, Klein Constantia and Constantia Uitsig before checking out the Cape Winelands around Stellenbosch, Paarl and Franschhoek. Stellenbosch has the added attraction of being an historical university town and Franschhoek, well established as the food capital of the Cape, is home to three of the country's top ten restaurants. The views are

voyage.name: Sunset cruise
voyage.content: On visiting Cape Town take the opportunity for a sunset cruise from one of the services lined up along the V&A dockside. Well worth seeing the sunset but also the view back towards the town and Table Mountain from the sea. Some tours include free wine and drinks, so you can get your sun-downer in as well. If you're lucky you may also see dolphins.

voyage.name: Swimming
voyage.content: Beaches on the False Bay side of the peninsula are the most popular with swimmers as the water is warmer. St James has the most picturesque tidal pool on the stretch between Muizenberg and Kalk Bay, while Clovelly and Fish Hoek beaches wrap around a sheltered bay with soft, white sands. Fishing boats, hobie cats and kayaks launch from here too. Brave hearts can sun-worship and swim naked in the freezing water of the

voyage.name: Surfing
voyage.content: Cape Town is one of the best places to surf. Muizenberg is a good place for beginners to learn to surf, Gary offers reasonably priced lessons from a shop facing the beach. Don't forget that the False Bay area (where Muizenberg is located in addition to Kalk Bay and Fish Hoek) is known for its sharks! If you're an experienced surfer, try the reef break at Kalk Bay, Outer Kom near Kommetjie or Misty Cliffs on the coast

voyage.name: Kite surfing
voyage.content: Cape Town is one of the most popular kite surfing destinations in the world. The two oceans, combined with the windy conditions, make for a great kite surfing experience. Some of the most popular kite surfing hot spots are Dolphin Beach in Blouberg Strand, Muizenberg and Langebaan Lagoon.

voyage.name: Newlands
voyage.content: Overlooked by Table Mountain and Devil's Peak, this scenic ground hosts Test matches and is home to Western Province and MI Cape Town teams. Its capacity is 20,000.

voyage.name: Ama Feesh Charters
voyage.price: Per charter, for inshore fishing, for offshore fishing, 1 to 6 people

voyage.name: Cape Charters
voyage.address: 31 Antigua, The Water Club, Granger Bay

voyage.name: Hooked on Africa
voyage.content: Tuna fishing charter that also offers boating excursions. If it's your lucky day, you'll catch a yellowfin.

voyage.name: SABP Tours
voyage.content: SABP Tours offers a diving opportunity to witness the great white shark.

voyage.name: Diving at Two Oceans Aquarium
voyage.price: ( if you bring your own diving gear), this includes the aquarium entrance fee
voyage.content: You must hold a recognised diving certification, specifically a minimum Open Water 1 qualification and present it when you arrive. Swim along with the sharks, guitar fish, bass, bull rays and turtles. The dive masters are kind and knowledgeable and will accompany you into the aquarium ready to fend off the sharks with his broomstick should they become cuddly. Dive time is around 30 minutes. For advanced divers, the K

voyage.name: Cape Argus Cycle Tour
voyage.price: Entrance fee is for entrants on the African continent or the equivalent of 50 EUR everyone else
voyage.content: Total distance is 109 km. Start in downtown, cycle down the eastern side of the peninsula, past Simon's Town and back up the western side of the peninsula.

voyage.name: Two Oceans Marathon
voyage.price: There is a pricing scale for each of the runs. The Ultra Marathon, for South African residents, for the rest of Africa and for the rest of the world. The Half Marathon, of South African residents, for the rest of Africa and for the rest of the world. The Fun Runs are priced from to
voyage.content: An Ultra marathon (56 km), a half marathon (21 km) and a number of fun runs ranging from a 56m Nappy Dash to a 8 km walk or run. Maximum 10 000 entrance accepted per year per race distance (fun runs excluded).

voyage.name: Cape Town Minstrel Carnival
voyage.hours: Usually New Years day and a couple of days later during January
voyage.address: Marches throughout the city ending at Green Point Stadium
voyage.content: Also known as the Kaapse Klopse, these brightly dressed singers and dancers spend months preparing for this annual event.

voyage.name: Kirstenbosch Summer Sunset Concerts
voyage.hours: late Nov to early April: Sun 17:30-18:30
voyage.address: Kirstenbosch Botanical Gardens Concert Stage, Rhodes Dr, Newlands
voyage.content: A picnic style concert, so bring a blanket and a picnic basket. Children under 6 years do not require a ticket. All concerts take place irrespective of rain. Regret no refunds are issued. The Kirstenbosch concerts are completely non-smoking events. There will be no designated smoking areas. Gates to the concert area open at 16h00 (On New Year’s Eve, gates open at 19h00).

voyage.name: Mother City Queer Project
voyage.price: to . The earlier you buy a ticket the cheaper it is
voyage.content: Biggest gay and lesbian party of the year.

voyage.name: First Thursdays
voyage.content: On the first Thursday of every month, walk between the galleries, restaurants and shops of Cape Town and Johannesburg until late.Discover the best things to see and places to go on First Thursdays. First Thursdays was started in Cape Town in 2012, and in Johannesburg in 2015. Inspired by similar initiatives in other cities around the world, the monthly event, taking place on the first Thursday of every month, is cent

voyage.name: The Cape of Good Hope Trail
voyage.content: Cape of Good Hope in the Table Mountain National Park, 34 km, 2 Days.

voyage.name: Hoerikwaggo Table Mountain Trail
voyage.content: 3-day, non-strenuous, luxury trail through the city, botanical gardens and Table Mountain National Park.

voyage.name: The Orangekloof Hiking Trail
voyage.content: 6 days, Cape Point to Table Mountain.

voyage.name: Table Mountain
voyage.hours: Always open, but you might want to start early enough to catch the last cable car down
voyage.content: 3 km (all uphill), 1 to 3 hours, Platteklip Gorge to the Upper Cable Station.

voyage.name: The Amphitheatre in the Kalk Bay mountains
voyage.content: 3 hours. Start at the sign on scenic Boyes Drive and climb up towards the rocks above which are peppered with scores of caves, many of which are not recommended for novice cavers so be careful. Take a torch. Follow the right forks in the trail and you'll be rewarded with increasingly spectacular views of False Bay. Head straight up through Echo Valley and through an ancient milkwood grove. Come back the same way if y

voyage.name: Paradise Touring
voyage.content: For guided walks up the mountain with a botanical guide.

voyage.name: Cape Eco-Tours
voyage.content: A good one for twitchers to use and is a member of Bird Life South Africa.

voyage.name: Trax Tours
voyage.content: Guided hiking and cycle tours in Franschoek and Stellenbosch, including wine tasting.

voyage.name: Meridian Hiking Club
voyage.content: This club organizes hikes ranging from easy day walks to strenuous rock scrambles on the mountain and multi-day hikes. Look up the calendar on the web site for details of current hikes. It is very popular with tourists.

voyage.name: Cape Town Helicopter Tours
voyage.content: Helicopter Wine Tours Western Cape, visit, Stellenbosch, Franschhoek and or Paarl from Cape Town.

voyage.name: NAC Helicopters
voyage.content: Offers chartered and private chopper rides.

voyage.name: Sport Helicopters
voyage.content: For scenic flights around the mountain, Huey flights, wine farm transfers.

voyage.name: ThunderCity
voyage.content: Go supersonic in a fighter jet.

voyage.name: Skydive Cape Town
voyage.content: One of the most scenic dropzones in the world, a 30 minutes drive up the just after Melkbos.

voyage.name: Para-Taxi
voyage.content: Paraglide over the Cape while being securely strapped to a professional pilot. Lovers of height will be blown away. Flights are also provided to the disabled.

voyage.name: Gravity Adventure Group
voyage.content: Provides training (African Paddling Association approved) as well as sea kayaking in the West Coast National Park.

voyage.name: Kaskazi Kayaks
voyage.content: Guided sea kayak trips, twice a day from Seapoint.

voyage.name: Waterfront Boat Company
voyage.content: Take a relaxing sunset cruise on the Condor to Greenpoint and back or do the champagne cruise. One to one and a half hours.

voyage.name: Tigger 2 Charters
voyage.price: From to per person depending on cruise

voyage.name: Jolly Roger Pirate Ship
voyage.price: from per child and per adult in winter, to
voyage.address: Jolly Roger Pirate Boat, Quay 5, V&A Waterfront
voyage.content: The Jolly Roger is the only authentic pirate ship in South Africa, departs from the V&A Waterfront at popular times. The Jolly Roger is able to sail in most weather conditions, normally at 11:00 (on weekends), 13:00, 15:00, 17:00 and 18:00. Must arrive early for boarding. Bookings to be made online here, or direct on arrival. https://www.webtickets.co.za/v2/EventCategories.aspx?itemid=379132481.

voyage.name: Andulela Tours
voyage.content: Offers a variety of different tours, including jazz, soccer, poetry, and culinary tours. Their emphasis is on meeting people, not looking at them.

voyage.name: Cape Fusion Tours
voyage.content: Offers hands-on African cooking experiences in Langa at a local cooking school. This gives you an insight into the culture, the people and their cuisine.

voyage.name: Kwathabeng Tours
voyage.content: Township Tavern Tours.

voyage.name: Luhambo Tours
voyage.content: Specialised in township tours (Gugulethu and Khayelitsha) and wine tours.

voyage.name: Taste the Cape Travel and Tours cc
voyage.content: A tour company specialising in wine and food tours with a registered tour guide.

voyage.name: Simon's Town Boat Company
voyage.content: The sole permit holder for boat based whale watching in False Bay (Permit No. 0806336). Also operate sightseeing cruises to Seal Island in the whale off-season.

voyage.name: Waterfront Boat Company
voyage.content: 3 to 4 hour cruise in the bay and you are almost guaranteed to spot whales.

voyage.name: Labia Theatre
voyage.content: An old-school cinema which has been open for more than 65 years.

voyage.name: Green Market Square
voyage.content: Originally a Farmers' Market dating back to 1710, Green Market is today one of the city's best flea markets. There's a range of local arts, craft and curios on offer and the vendors expect to bargain for their wares.

voyage.name: Caroline's Fine Wines
voyage.address: V&A Waterfront and 15 Long Street in the City Centre
voyage.content: Better selection and more knowledgeable staff. City Centre location recommended, but both are excellent. Foam inserts and boxes for international shipping or for checking with your luggage (safe!) Not cheap though, compared to supermarkets and wineries.

voyage.name: Vaughan Johnson's Wine Shop
voyage.content: Quality selection but not exhaustive. Knowledgeable staff. Generally substantial (10-20%) markup over winery prices but of course more convenient.

voyage.name: Wine Concepts
voyage.address: Cardiff Castle Building, cnr Main Street & Kildare Road, Newlands (Southern Suburbs)
voyage.content: Another great wine shop, certainly the best outside the City Bowl. A franchised location is on Kloof Street in the Lifestyle Centre.

voyage.name: Ultra
voyage.content: A large South African liquor chain. Several locations around the city, the one in Green Point is the most accessible to tourists. A warehouse bottle store but with a remarkable wine selection across all price ranges. Case discount (even on mixed cases). Good if you want to stock up for a road trip. Stash a bottle of Amarula Cream in your backpack while you're at it. Great prices -- in fact, often cheaper than at the

voyage.name: Blue Route Mall
voyage.address: cnr Tokai and Keyser River Roads, Tokai

voyage.name: Constantia Village
voyage.address: cnr Constantia Main and Spaanschemacht River Roads, Constantia

voyage.name: Kenilworth Centre
voyage.address: cnr Doncaster and Chichester Roads, Kenilworth

voyage.name: Maynard Mall
voyage.address: cnr Main and Wetton Roads, Wynberg

voyage.name: N1 City
voyage.address: Louwtjie Rothman Drive (off Monte Vista Boulevard), Goodwood

voyage.name: Tyger Valley
voyage.address: cnr Bill Bezuidenhout and Willie van Schoor Avenues, Bellville

voyage.name: Victoria & Alfred Waterfront
voyage.content: Has a Pick N Pay supermarket.

voyage.name: Golden Acre Shopping Centre
voyage.content: many low prices shops and places to eat right in down town cape town. has a Pep Clothing/shoe Store

voyage.name: Canal Walk Shopping Centre
voyage.content: Cape Town’s largest shopping centre has over 400 stores.

voyage.name: Pep stores
voyage.content: low cost clothing and shoes.

voyage.name: The Book Lounge
voyage.content: Independent bookshop focusing on South African works but with a good range of international books as well. Runs a busy program of book launches and other events. Often identified as one of the best, or the best, bookshops in South Africa.

voyage.name: Clarke's Bookshop
voyage.content: This long-standing bookshop has two stories of books, with a mix of new and second-hand works.

voyage.name: Exclusive Books, V&A Waterfront
voyage.content: This large branch of the national Exclusive Books chain is conveniently located for tourists in the V&A Waterfront mall. It has sections for South African fiction and non-fiction works (including a dedicated area for books about Nelson Mandela!). There are other branches of the chain located across Cape Town, including at the airport.

voyage.name: Eastern Food Bazaar
voyage.content: South Asian food court offering high quality meals for a fair price. 100% Halal.

voyage.name: Best Of Asia Green Point
voyage.content: Sushi

voyage.name: The Charles
voyage.price: From for small English breakfast (served with toasted white or whole wheat bread) 1 egg, rasher bacon, sausage, fried tomato and sauté mushrooms
voyage.content: The Charles can accommodate 25–30 people seated.

voyage.name: Africa Café
voyage.content: Affordable and very good. Maybe the best restaurant in Cape Town for African cuisine. Lower to medium price range. Serves fixed menu, all you can eat of 12-15 different dishes.

voyage.name: Biesmiellah
voyage.content: One of the oldest restaurants around, known for its Malay kitchen. No alcoholic drinks are available.

voyage.name: Col'Cacchio Pizzeria
voyage.address: 42 Hans Strijdom Avenue Foreshore (also at Eden on the Bay in Bloubergstrand)
voyage.content: Italian dishes made to order.

voyage.name: 95 Keerom
voyage.content: A top class Italian restaurant with modern décor and a trendy atmosphere.

voyage.name: Lolas
voyage.content: Vegetarian food with local colour and great karma. Good conversation and even better meals. Mingle with dreadlocks, artsy types and brooding poets.

voyage.name: Long Street Café
voyage.content: Very popular, European kitchen, which serves up tasty drinks.

voyage.name: Mama Africa
voyage.hours: Mon to Sat: restaurant is open 19:00 till late, the bar is open 16:30 till late
voyage.content: African style tourist restaurant offering local and African meals, like Bobotie and Potjiekos, but also springbok, kudu and crocodile steak. Good range of wines at affordable prices. Live marimba music some nights.

voyage.name: Willoughby's
voyage.content: Has some of the best seafood including excellent sushi at very good prices.

voyage.name: Table Mountain Restaurant
voyage.hours: 08:30 to 18:30, with extended hours during December and January
voyage.address: On top of Table Mountain, close to the Upper Cable Station
voyage.content: Temporarily closed as of August 2022. A 120 seat, self-service restaurant. No booking required. Quality is variable.

voyage.name: Tide
voyage.content: Serving with steamed seasonal vegetables, new potatoes and lemon butter.

voyage.name: Stardust Theatrical Dining
voyage.content: While eating delicious Mediterranean cuisine, customers are entertained by their talented waitrons who perform throughout the evening between serving tables.

voyage.name: Greek Fisherman
voyage.content: Choose from authentic Mediterranean tapas and a wide range of seafood and meat from the open flame grill.

voyage.name: City Grill Steakhouse
voyage.content: Enjoy delicious selection of traditional South African steaks, grills and venison.

voyage.name: Meloncino
voyage.content: Choose from a variety of homemade pastas, wood-fired pizzas and various other authentic dishes.

voyage.name: La Colombe
voyage.content: La Colombe, one of Cape Town's most well-loved and awarded restaurants, achieved an impressive 12th place in the San Pellegrino 50 Best Restaurants of the World Awards 2010. Having moved up 26 places and into the hallowed Top 20, this bastion of contemporary French-meets-Asian fine dining thereby also clinched the Acqua Panna Best Restaurant in Africa and Middle East Award. Winner of Chef of the Year and Restaurant o

voyage.name: The Test Kitchen
voyage.address: The Old Biscuit Mill 375 Albert Road Woodstock
voyage.content: Luke Dale-Roberts’ The Test Kitchen, which opened in 2010, has the celebrated chef cooking at his most creative in a distinctive contemporary space. At the prestigious World’s 50 Best Restaurants Awards 2013, The Test Kitchen made an impressive leap to No. 61 on the list, climbing up 13 places from no.74 in 2012. More significantly, The Test Kitchen was singled out as the winner of the “Cacao Barry One To Watch Award

voyage.name: Bobs Bar
voyage.content: A British-owned and -run bar with beer from . and breakfast from .

voyage.name: Club 169
voyage.content: A dance club and cigar bar focusing on hip hop and RnB music.

voyage.name: Foresters Arms
voyage.content: Nestled at the foot of our majestic mountains, in the leafy suburb of Newlands, Cape Town, Foresters Arms Restaurant and Pub (fondly referred to by the locals as Forries), is one of the oldest pubs in South Africa and provides a retreat from the hustle and bustle of city life. They have a good selection of draught beers.

voyage.name: Marco's African Place
voyage.content: Popular gay bar which serves up specialities such as Ulwimi (steamed ox tongue with mustard sauce) along with live African music.

voyage.name: Mitchells Ale House
voyage.address: Cnr East Pier & Dock Road V&A Waterfront
voyage.content: Great location, fun atmosphere, friendly staff and famous craft beers, amazing views of the Cape Town harbour and Table Mountain, and karaoke.

voyage.name: Sandy B
voyage.content: Open to the public at The Bay Hotel over summer, Sandy B is a unique cocktail venue, accentuated by its glorious views of Camps Bay beachfront.

voyage.name: Zanzi-Bar
voyage.content: Run by the Carnival Court Backpackers hostel. Good meeting place for other travelers visiting Cape Town. Live jazz on Sundays, DJ's on Friday & Saturday nights. Free entry most nights.

voyage.name: Fiction Bar
voyage.content: Renowned club with weekly indie-, drum'n'bass- and minimal-electro-nights

voyage.name: Mercury Live & Lounge
voyage.content: World-class live music, with students nights.

voyage.name: Liziwe's Bed and Breakfast
voyage.content: Township B&B.

voyage.name: Ma Neo's B&B
voyage.content: Township B&B.

voyage.name: 33 South Backpackers
voyage.content: A boutique-style hostel. You can join them every Tuesday for their locally known "creative evening.".

voyage.name: African HeART BAckpackers
voyage.content: African HeART is an artwork in progress, a small, beautifully decorated backpackers which aims to offer the alternative side to travelling in Cape Town.

voyage.name: Anzac Backpackers
voyage.content: Dorm beds and twin rooms has a kitchen, travel desk, big screen TV, bicycles for hire, airport transfers, fast Wi-Fi included.

voyage.name: Ashanti Lodge
voyage.content: A perennial favourite among travellers; camping also permitted. Has a large travel centre as well.

voyage.name: A Sunflower Stop Backpackers
voyage.content: Tastefully decorated perfectly and clean dorms. Doubles and twins. En-suite rooms available too.

voyage.name: Backpackers on Castle
voyage.content: Dorm beds and double rooms.

voyage.name: Big Blue Backpackers
voyage.content: A clean hostel with dorm beds. Free Wi-Fi, swimming pool, free tea and coffee 07:00–10:00.

voyage.name: Castle Inn Backpackers
voyage.content: Directly opposite the Castle of Good Hope and 5 minutes' walk from the train station. Cheapest Internet cafe in the area.

voyage.name: Light House farm Lodge
voyage.price: dorm beds per day per person
voyage.address: Oude Molen Eco Village Alexandra road

voyage.name: Long Street Backpackers
voyage.content: Right in the heart of the party street. Has a bar. Offers dorms.

voyage.name: Never@Home Backpackers
voyage.price: Dorm beds from per person sharing
voyage.content: Vibrant and colourful youth hostel with all amenities. The rooms are private or shared dorms from 4 beds upwards and ensuite. Communal kitchen and lounge area with bar and glittering pool upstairs with a terrace and reasonable pool bar. There is Wi-Fi and sanitation stations, masks are compulsory.

voyage.name: Riverlodge Backpackers
voyage.address: oude molen eco village Alexandria road Pinelands
voyage.content: Has camping and a 10-bed dorm.

voyage.name: Two Oceans Backpackers
voyage.content: Dorms and private rooms. Linen provided, hostel is very clean and staff friendly and there is a bar and balcony to hang out.

voyage.name: 26 on Aandbloem
voyage.price: single, pps (includes breakfast, en-suit bathroom with shower & WC)
voyage.content: Views of Table Mountain and the Cape Town City Bowl.

voyage.name: Abbey Manor Luxury Guesthouse
voyage.content: Luxury guesthouse set high on Table Mountain overlooking Cape Town city. Dramatic views from individually decorated rooms. Built in 1905 in the Arts-and-Crafts style, and has been remodelled. An easy hop from the city centre and the V&A Waterfront. Rated 5 stars by TGCSA. Provides free wi-fi to guests.

voyage.name: The Bay Atlantic Guest House
voyage.content: Beautiful four star guest house in Camps Bay with exhausting view on the beach of Camps Bay and the Lionshead, only 10 minutes away from the V&A Waterfront. Provides free wi-fi to guests.

voyage.name: Bayflowers Guest House
voyage.price: from for a single room, pps for a double
voyage.content: Very central, walk to Waterfront, beach and city centre, helpful staff, rooms clean and tastefully equipped.

voyage.name: Cactusberry Lodge
voyage.content: 3 star. 200 metres from the Gardens Shopping Centre, is comfortable, central and quiet, very good value for money, excellent breakfast, very helpful in all itinerary planning.

voyage.name: The Camps Bay Guesthouse
voyage.content: Exclusive use of 180 m² private self-catering stand alone luxury accommodation set in the grounds of the owners Camps Bay Villa, private and secure with onsite gated parking, full kitchen, teak floors, living and dining room with underfloor heating throughout, widescreen LCD television with Apple TV entertainment system and stereo surround, complimentary hi-speed WIFI access, private deck and garden area opens into t

voyage.name: Cape Diamond Boutique Hotel
voyage.content: All rooms equipped with air-conditioning, private toilet and bath, safe deposit box, side lamp table and Wired Internet connection (extra charges apply). Some of its facilities and services are meeting/ banquet facilities, business centre, restaurant, Theatre Cafe, 24-hour front desk, room service and laundry service.

voyage.name: Cape Paradise Lodge
voyage.content: Has Table Mountain as a backdrop and fantastic views.

voyage.name: The Charles Guesthouse
voyage.price: for single room, for a double
voyage.content: Trendy and fashionable today, it is compared to New York's Greenwich Village and London's Soho with its tree-lined streets, restored cottages, spectacular views and village atmosphere.

voyage.name: City Lodge V&A Waterfront
voyage.content: 3 star.

voyage.name: Daddy Long Legs Boutique Hotel & Self-Catering Apartments
voyage.price: From a double/twin (hotel) & a one bedroomed apartment
voyage.content: Located in the heart of the city centre on one of Cape Town's most celebrated streets - a hotel with a difference, focusing on good value accommodation and a hotel experience you'll never forget.

voyage.name: Dark Chocolate Guest House Durbanville
voyage.content: Standard rooms, all equipped with Air-conditioning, TV with cable and High-speed Internet connection. Facilities and services are garden, outdoor swimming pool and conference.

voyage.name: De Waterkant Village
voyage.price: for single room, for a double
voyage.content: De Waterkant is often described as being arty, charismatic and quaint and is a truly special place decorated with gorgeous al fresco restaurants, sidewalk café's, boutiques and bars and is often compared with Greenwich Village.

voyage.name: Don Beach Road Hotel
voyage.content: The Don Beach Road is located in Sea Point spectacularly overlooking the Atlantic Ocean.

voyage.name: Grande Kloof Boutique Hotel
voyage.price: from (includes light continental breakfast, free WIFI, open plan top floor sea view rooms or executive petite garden level rooms, swimming pool, jacuzzi area, steam area, sauna
voyage.content: Good sea views, Fantastic Lions head view and views of famous Robben Island.

voyage.name: Kloof Nek Suites
voyage.content: Kloof Nek Suites is a guest house offering three self-catering rooms in Tamboerskloof.

voyage.name: Lorraine’s on Lincoln
voyage.content: All rooms equipped with English breakfast, Spacious dining area, Hair dryer, TV with satellite channels, Work desk and Fan. Outdoor swimming pool, Garden, Banquet hall, Car rental, Wi-Fi Internet connection, Fax and photocopying services.

voyage.name: Nine Flowers Guest House
voyage.price: for a single room to for a triple
voyage.content: Very central, helpful staff, nice rooms.

voyage.name: The One 8
voyage.content: Modern and intimate Four star accommodation in Cape Town. The One 8 Hotel is located in Green Point and close to Clifton Beach, Camps Bay, V&A Waterfront, De Waterkant gay village, and Table Mountain. This gay and lesbian friendly Guest House offers bed and breakfast and contemporary rooms for your South African Holiday.

voyage.name: Protea Hotel Sea Point
voyage.content: Protea has a whole bunch of hotels in Cape Town and surrounding areas. It is well worth checking their website for last-minute bargains, which can reduce the price by 50%.

voyage.name: Rhonda's Manor
voyage.content: Upper Sea Point, near the Waterfront, Campsbay and Clifton beaches.

voyage.name: Southern Light Country House
voyage.content: Southern Light Country House is an accommodation in Constantia set in the beautiful surround of Upper Constantia.

voyage.name: Tudor Hotel
voyage.price: for single room, for a double
voyage.content: In the city centre, near the Waterfront, Parliament, Gardens or the Malay Quarter Boo-Kap.

voyage.name: Villa Sunshine Guesthouse
voyage.content: The Villa Sunshine guesthouse is a classic Mediterranean Villa situated along the prestigious Atlantic Seaboard. In close proximity to several of Cape Town’s most revered tourist attractions, it is still able to provide its guests with a peaceful setting – within walking distance of restaurants and shops to meet your every need.

voyage.name: Villa Zest Boutique Hotel
voyage.content: The Villa Zest is in the Green Point suburb.

voyage.name: Cape Grace
voyage.address: West Quay Road, Victoria & Alfred Waterfront
voyage.content: Situated on its own private quay on Cape Town’s vibrant Victoria and Alfred Waterfront, the Cape Grace has 121 rooms all with views of the V&A harbour or yacht marina with a Table Mountain backdrop.

voyage.name: De Verdwaalde Boer
voyage.alt: private villa & guesthouse with Dutch management. #1 at Booking.com and #1 at Tripadvisor
voyage.content: De Verdwaalde Boer boasts 7 suites and is available to book as a villa for full privacy.

voyage.name: Mandela Rhodes Place
voyage.content: Old school charm and hospitality meets modern amenities and features. It also boasts a gymnasium, swimming pool, wireless internet, undercover parking, 24 hour concierge and business centre, optional breakfast service, pre-delivery grocery shopping, airport and city transfers, car hire, housekeeping and laundry and day tours

voyage.name: Mount Nelson
voyage.content: Opened in 1899, as the first hotel in South Africa to offer hot and cold running water.

voyage.name: Radisson Blu Hotel Waterfront, Cape Town
voyage.content: 5-star hotel overlooking its own private marina and the famous Robben Island.

voyage.name: Southern Light Guest House
voyage.content: Upmarket bed and breakfast.
